verdict: TRANSCRIPTION RATE (88695 gene-celltype pairs, 8 cell lines): computes the quantity this project had been discussing without ever calculating. RNAdecayCafe carries both steady-state abundance and measured decay constant per gene per cell line, and at steady state k_syn = RPKM * k_deg, so the absolute synthesis rate follows directly in RPKM per hour -- no modelling required. In K562 the median gene is transcribed at 3.42 RPKM/h and rates span 4.6 orders of magnitude. AN EQUATION was then fitted to log10 k_syn from promoter structure, gene class and regulatory wiring, scored on HELD-OUT GENES, with expression, protein abundance and any other level-carrying feature EXCLUDED because k_syn is built from abundance and would otherwise be trivially predictable. Nested layers, K562: promoter alone R2=0.157, plus gene class 0.207, plus how many TFs regulate the gene 0.216, plus which 1213 specific TFs 0.153, and a gradient-boosted fit on the same features 0.322. TF IDENTITY IS WORTH -0.0630 R2 over merely counting regulators, which is the honest answer to whether regulatory wiring carries rate information. WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not 'TF X boosts gene Y by Z-fold'. No TF is manipulated anywhere in this data; the 13 cell lines differ in thousands of ways simultaneously, so the TF-identity layer measures association between wiring and rate, not the causal effect of any single factor. Getting that would need a TF induction series with nascent-RNA readout, which is not on disk. Deterministic.
